claim_scope: Exact static implementation, real host CLI, real Docker Compose configuration render, normalized security projection, copy-only Dockerfiles, migration and runner source self-tests, and fail-closed implementation mutations. No image was built and no container, network, volume, PostgreSQL, migration, or runner runtime was started.
implemented_surfaces: compose.yaml with PostgreSQL, migration, Python runner, and Node runner
Standard-library-only Python and Node runners with bounded PostgreSQL v3 clients
Exact topology implementation lock and stable redacted-model digest

checks.result: The Windows checkout launcher returned exactly one schema-valid incidentseal-cli-envelope/v1 result with command topology.validate, verdict PASS, and exit 0.
Docker Compose 5.1.3 rendered the actual compose.yaml; its redacted model digest repeated exactly and its normalized security projection matched the frozen fixture.
Compose, migration, both runners, all Dockerfiles, the runner fixture, CLI dispatch, and topology validator matched the exact implementation lock.

All three contexts contain only their declared files and use exact Dockerfile frontend and exact base references with allowed copy/configure instructions; RUN, ADD, network, package resolution, secret, and SSH inputs are absent.

The real render preserves numeric users, read-only roots, no-new-privileges, cap_drop ALL, PID limits, no published ports, one internal network, staged mounts, exact commands, dependencies, healthcheck, tmpfs, and evidence labels.
Host Python and Node source self-tests produced the same canonical request digest and distinct runner result digests without accessing PostgreSQL.
All 41 unit tests passed, including three topology parser and runner-source tests.
The original machine-contract validator and mutations plus the topology-contract validator and its 12 mutations remained PASS.
All 13 recomputed-lock or stale-lock mutations failed with the expected IS_TOPOLOGY_RENDER or IS_TOPOLOGY_IMPLEMENTATION code.
Container history was unchanged across validation; no IncidentSeal container, network, volume, or derived image exists.

retained_attempts.note: The first model digest included random generated staging paths and differed between otherwise identical invocations. It was not accepted as stable evidence. The final path-redacted model repeated at sha256:ac5ff46425265cba08e249a1c7ace47908ab9b1726db8dccf557178fd5d2f89c.

The first temporary-copy harness omitted the locked runner request fixture and correctly failed with IS_TOPOLOGY_READ at exit 74. The copy scope was repaired; baseline and all 13 mutations then passed.

decision.next_action: Through the host CLI, build the three copy-only derived images with no build network, bind their actual local image IDs in a runtime lock, rerender against the contract, then start only the platform-validation topology and probe the complete runtime security surface.
prohibited_claims: No derived image has been built or assigned a real runtime identity.
No container, PostgreSQL server, migration, Python runner, or Node runner has executed.
No workflow manifest is approved or eligible to execute.
No database, runner, persistence, recovery, dashboard, clean-clone topology, image publication, or release behavior has been verified.
